actions.body: Analysis of the collected literature [source-bda2bc47c38c47a2, source-db145486024f469a, source-f955850b0fcf467a] indicates that cognitive architecture design remains heavily focused on standardized categorical frameworks. While these frameworks provide foundational structural mappings, internal mechanisms for robust self-correction or explicit error detection in reasoning remain less unified. The synthesis confirms that evolutionary patterns in AI agent design currently emphasize real-world applicability over standardized metacognitive self-correction processes. Future work requires distinguishing between architectural self-monitoring (system-level) and agentic self-reflection (reasoning-level).
actions.lede: This review synthesizes consensus on cognitive architecture structures and examines emerging literature on self-monitoring, error detection, and model self-correction.
actions.reason: Resolving the commitment to synthesize literature into the revised notebook p-reasoning-limits-001.
actions.title: Provisional Review: Architectural Consensus and Self-Monitoring
